Content

Cause of Origin

  • Brahminical domination: Jainism and Buddhism were against the ritualistic interpretation of Vedas and opposed Brahminical Domination.
  • Agricultural Economy: Trade was impacted due to ritualistic sacrifices. Trade was carried out by Vaishyas.
  • Punch marked coins: Use of punch marked coins started.
  • Varna System: Jainism and Buddhism did not attach themselves to Varna system and everyone treated equally. Jainism believed Varnas were on the basis of occupation and not by birth.
  • Belief in Non-violence: Both the religions believed in path of Ahimsa.
  • Mahavir and Buddha were Kshatriyas.
  • Jainism and Buddhism are considered "heterodox" in context of Indian philosophy (It means that they do not accept the authority of the Vedas, unlike orthodox Hindu traditions).
  • Worship: Jainism believed in divine figure however Buddhism did not.

JAINISM

  • In Jainism, Tirthankaras are considered to be great teachers.
  • There are total 24 Tirthankaras.

  • In Vedas, only two Tirthankaras are mentioned: Rishabh Dev (1st) and Arishtanemi (22nd).

Vardhaman Mahavir

  • Birth: 540 BC (approx.); Kundagram (Vaishali; Bihar).
  • Death: 468 BC; Pavapuri (Bihar); during the age of 72 years.
  • Father: Siddhartha (Clan: Jnatrika; he was a Kshatriya).
  • Wife: Yashoda
  • Daughter: Priyadarshana (also known as Anoja) who married Jamali (he was the first disciple of Mahavir).
  • Mahavir left home at the age of 30 years; along with Makkhali Gosala.
  • Enlightenment: At the age of 42 years; under a Sal tree at Jambhikagrama near river Rijupalika.
  • First Sermon at: Vipulachala mountain near Rajgriha (Rajgir), Bihar (corrected: Pava, Kushinagar → Rajgriha, Bihar — Mahavira died at Pavapuri near Nalanda, but his first sermon was at Rajgriha).

Ajivika Sect

  • Founder: Makkhali Gosala
  • This sect believed in extreme fatalism (fate) and asceticism (living extreme form of life by abstinence from worldly pleasure).

Jain Philosophy (Triratnas)

  • According to Jainism, three principles to achieve Moksha:

| K | Right Knowledge (Samyaka Jnana) |

| F | Right Faith (Samyaka Darshana) |

| C | Right Conduct (Samyaka Charitra) |

Division among Jains

  • Chandragupta Maurya and Bhadrabahu left Magadha for Karnataka due to severe famine in Magadha and settled in Shravanabelagola, where Chandragupta Maurya embraced Jainism. He eventually undertook Sallekhana (ritual fasting) and passed away. Meanwhile, another group of Jains chose to remain in Magadha under the leadership of Sthulabhadra.
  • Overtime, differences arose between these two groups.
  • The followers of Bhadrabahu, who migrated to the South, adhered to strict ascetic practices, including nudity as a mark of renunciation, and came to be known as Digambaras (sky-clad).
  • On the other hand, the Jains who stayed in Magadha, led by Sthulabhadra, adopted more liberal monastic rules, permitting monks to wear white clothes. This group became known as Shwetambaras (white-clad).

BUDDHISM

Gautam Buddha

  • He belonged to: Shakya Clan.
  • He was also known as Shakyamuni, Tathagat.
  • Birth: 563 BC; Lumbini, Nepal
  • Death: 483 BC; Kushinagara, Uttar Pradesh
  • Childhood name: Siddhartha
  • Father: Suddhodhana
  • Mother: Mahamaya (belonged to Koliya tribe).
  • Step-mother: Mahaprajapati Goutami (first Bhikkhuni).
  • Wife: Yashodhara
  • Son: Rahul
  • Buddha left home at the age of 29 years.
  • First teacher: Alara Kalama
  • Second teacher: Udraka Ramputra
  • Enlightenment: Uruvela (Bodh Gaya); under a Bodhi tree (peepal tree) for 49 days near river Niranjana.
  • First sermon: Sarnath; Varanasi
  • Gautam Buddha is considered as "Light of Asia".

Philosophy of Buddhism

There are four noble truths:

  1. 1. The truth of suffering.
  2. 2. The truth of the cause of suffering (i.e., desire).
  3. 3. The truth of the end of suffering.
  4. 4. The truth of the path to the end of suffering (i.e. Eight Fold Path).

Eight Fold Path or Ashtangika Marga

It is followed to end sufferings.

  • Right mindfulness
  • Right view
  • Right intention
  • Right concentration
  • Right speech
  • Right action
  • Right effort
  • Right livelihood

In 4th Buddhist Council, Buddhism was divided into two sects: Mahayana and Hinayana.

Buddhist Texts

  • Sutta pitaka: Buddha's teachings / sermons.
  • Vinaya pitaka: Monastic courts and rules.
  • Abhidhamma pitaka: Interpretation of Suttapitaka.
  • Theravada Buddhism origin: India
  • Pitaka meaning: Basket

In Pali Language

  • Milindpanho: Dialogue between Milinda (Indo-Greek King Menander I) and Nagasena.

Bodhisattvas

  • A Bodhisattva is a being who seeks enlightenment (Bodhi) not just for themselves, but for the benefit of all sentient beings. The concept is central to Mahayana Buddhism, where Bodhisattvas delay their own Nirvana to help others attain liberation.

Some well-known Bodhisattvas include:

  • Padmapani: A bodhisattva who is also known as Avalokiteshwara.
  • Vajrapani: A bodhisattva who is a protector and a guide.
  • Manjusri: A bodhisattva who represents wisdom and is considered the Buddha-to-be.

In Sanskrit Language

  • Buddhacharitra: Buddha's biography by Asvaghosha.
  • Jataka tales: it is about previous births of Buddha in both human and animal forms.

Sanchi Stupa

  • It is the oldest Stupa of India built by King Ashoka in 3rd Century BC.
  • The carving on Stupa was done using Sandstone by Shunga Dynasty.
  • It has four Gateways which represent cardinal points → North, South, West and East direction.
  • First discovered by: Henry Taylor in 1818.
  • Chethiyagiri festival is celebrated at Sanchi.
  • Relics of two important disciples of Buddha → Sariputta and Moggallana are kept here.

Parts of a Stupa

  • Anda: Hemispherical dome
  • Torana: Gateway
  • Medhi: Pedestrian Path (raised circular terrace)
  • Vedika: Railings
  • Pradakshina patha: A circular path around stupa where devotees walk around
